newsitem.title: EGYPT: EgyptAir to fly Libya pilgrims to Saudi Arabia.
newsitem.headline: EgyptAir to fly Libya pilgrims to Saudi Arabia.

text.p: EgyptAir will fly 11,000 Libyans to Saudi Arabia for the annual Moslem haj pilgrimage in Mecca later this month, an airline official said on Friday.

Ahmed Shawki told reporters EgyptAir would begin the first of 45 flights to Libya on March 30 and end them on April 11. The flights would pick up pilgrims from the Libyan capital Tripoli and the eastern port of Benghazi, he said.

Libya is under a United Nations air embargo that forbids all flights in an out of the country, but a U.N. Security Council commission on Thursday approved EgyptAir to transport Libyans to Saudi Arabia on 45 flights.

The U.N. imposed flight sanctions on Libya in 1992 for failing to hand over two Libyan suspects for trial in the United States or Britain for the 1988 bombing of a Pan Am plane over Lockerbie, Scotland, that killed 270 people.
All flights must be nonstop between the authorised destinations and none of the planes used may be owned by or leased from Libya, which is not to gain financially from the flights.

Libya has occasionally violated the sanctions. The last occasion was in January when a Libyan plane, without U.N. permission, flew an official delegation to Accra, Ghana. The sanctions committee has asked Libya for an explanation.
